selectWorld.trulyrandom.loot_tables.tool: Randomises the loot tables of blocks, entities, chests and more.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.recipes.tooltip: Randomises the crafting recipes of items.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.structures.toolt:
Each structure will be replaced with a different structure where it would generate (excluding strongholds).
Eg: Shipwreck placed instead of an outpost.
§c/locate will be unreliable.
Cannot be changed once set.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.features.tooltip:
Each features will be replaced with another feature where possible.
Eg: Iceberg placed instead of a tree.
§cCannot be changed once set.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.block_palette.to:
Each type of block will be replaced with another type of block.
Eg: Oak Leaves are replaced with Stone Stairs.
§cWarning: May Lead to Unstable Worlds.
Cannot be changed once set.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.trades.tooltip:
Randomises the traded items of villagers.
This includes emeralds.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.seed.title: Seed:
selectWorld.trulyrandom.seed.tooltip: Seed that will be used to determine the randomisation.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.block_models_set:
Force all instances of a block state to share the same model as the default state.
For example all fences would use the same fence model regardless of the number of connections they have.

Ignoring model occlussion can cause solid blocks to be replaced with non-solid block models allowing you to see through the world, which can cause significant FPS lag as no culling will be applied to these blocks.
Ignoring state properties can cause blocks to use any model with the same occlusion shape, which can make tracking what is what significantly more difficult and rendering quirks are to be expected.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.item_model_setti:
If possible force the random item model to use the same random block model when block model randomisation is enabled.
This ignores the seed provided to the item model randomisation module.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.loot_settings.us: Whether the randomisation should swap loot tables or produce random items with a random quantity. Swapping loot tables is the default and is recommended as it allows for more consistent randomisation and better compatibility with other mods. Disabling also disables the tracker as it would be redundant.
selectWorld.trulyrandom.structure_settin: The legacy randomiser simply allowed all structures to generate everywhere, this was not "random". The new randomiser replaces what structure is generated when a structure is asked to be generated, which causes more structure overlap and corruption.
Whether the elytra in end cities is replaced by one that has 0 durability to prevent easy access to flight when end city ships generate everywhere
selectWorld.trulyrandom.block_palette_se: Ignoring state properties allows non-similar blocks to be picked, ie log types can be replaced with non-orientable blocks such as stones, which would not normally be allowed. This can make the world significantly harder to navigate and gather resources in.
Ignoring the collision shape can lead to tricky terrain to navigate, either by stone being replaced with a wall type block or a non-full-cube block like a door.
Ignoring the occlusion shape can cause solid blocks to be replaced with non-solid blocks which may cause rendering or performance issues.

Prevents stone-like blocks from being replaced with a different block. This will allow surface rules to apply to the overworld which would typically fail and prevent dirt, grass, ores, etc from being placed, which also prevents most features from being placed.
